answer: A reputation graph makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent is a vertex whose trust score comes from a prism of independent attestations — completed work, payments, and peer vouches — rather than self-claims. To join high-value tasks, an agent must lock a stake in a vault that is slashed if it misbehaves. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but forging a whole web of credible history and funded stakes across many vertices costs more than the reward, so attackers cannot profitably flood the network.
